items.informal_name: Monomial Preservation under Inverse Algebra Equivalence
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] {d : PUnit.{1} →₀ ℕ} {r : R},
  (MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm ((Polynomial.monomial (d ())) r) = (MvPolynomial.monomial d) r
items.informal_description: The inverse of the algebra equivalence between multivariate polynomials over the unit type $\mathsf{PUnit}$ and univariate polynomials maps a monomial $rX^d$ in the univariate ring $R[X]$ to the corresponding monomial $rX^d$ in the multivariate ring $R[\mathsf{PUnit}]$. Specifically, for any coefficient $r \in R$ and degree $d \in \mathbb{N}$, applying the inverse equivalence to the univariate monomial yields the multivariate monomial with the same coefficient and degree.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Polynomial to Power Series Conversion with pUnit Algebra Equivalence
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {f : Polynomial R}, ↑f = ↑((MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm f)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f $ over a ring $ R $, the direct conversion of $ f $ to a univariate power series coincides with the conversion obtained by first applying the algebra isomorphism between multivariate polynomials over the unit type $ \mathsf{PUnit} $ and univariate polynomials, then converting to a multivariate power series. Formally, $ f.toPowerSeries = ((\mathsf{pUnitAlgEquiv}.symm\, f).toMvPowerSeries) $, where $ \mathsf{pUnitAlgEquiv} $ denotes the canonical algebra equivalence.

items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, the algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ (where $ \mathsf{PUnit} $ is the unit type with one element) and the univariate polynomial ring $ R[X] $ maps the monomial $ \mathsf{monomial}(d, r) $ in $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ to the monomial $ rX^{d()} $ in $ R[X] $, where $ d $ is a finite support function encoding the single exponent.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials over Unit Type
items.type:

items.informal_description: The inverse of the algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ and the univariate polynomial ring $ R[X] $ maps a polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ to its representation in $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ by substituting the indeterminate $ X $ with the single variable $ X(\mathsf{PUnit}.\mathsf{unit}) $ in the multivariate ring, using the constant polynomial embedding $ \mathsf{C} $ for coefficients.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Polynomial-Finitely Supported Function Isomorphism is Identity
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] (toFinsupp : AddMonoidAlgebra R ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.toFinsuppIsoAlg R).symm toFinsupp).toFinsupp = toFinsupp
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $ and any finitely supported function $ f : \mathbb{N} \to R $, applying the inverse of the canonical $ R $-algebra isomorphism from $ R[\mathbb{N}] $ to $ R[X] $ and then converting back to a finitely supported function results in $ f $ itself. This asserts that the composition of the inverse isomorphism and the finitely supported function conversion is the identity function on $ R[\mathbb{N}] $.

∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] {d : PUnit.{1} →₀ ℕ} {r : R},
  (MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm ((Polynomial.monomial (d ())) r) = (MvPolynomial.monomial d) r
items.informal_description: The inverse of the algebra equivalence between multivariate polynomials over the unit type $\mathsf{PUnit}$ and univariate polynomials maps a monomial $rX^d$ in the univariate ring $R[X]$ to the corresponding monomial $rX^d$ in the multivariate ring $R[\mathsf{PUnit}]$. Specifically, for any coefficient $r \in R$ and degree $d \in \mathbb{N}$, applying the inverse equivalence to the univariate monomial yields the multivariate monomial with the same coefficient and degree.

items.informal_description: Given commutative semirings $ R $ and $ S_3 $, and types $ S_1, S_2 $, if ring homomorphisms $ f : R[S_1] → S_3[S_2] $ and $ g : S_3[S_2] → R[S_1] $ satisfy $ f ∘ g $ and $ g ∘ f $ preserving constant polynomials and mapping variables to themselves, then the inverse of the ring equivalence $ R[S_1] ≃+* S_3[S_2] $ is given by $ g $. Specifically, for any polynomial $ a ∈ S_3[S_2] $, the inverse equivalence evaluates to $ g(a) $.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Multivariate Polynomial Ring Equivalence via Algebra Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} (σ : Type u_1) [inst : CommSemiring R] {A₁ : Type u_2} {A₂ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : CommSemiring A₁]
  [inst_2 : CommSemiring A₂] [inst_3 : Algebra R A₁] [inst_4 : Algebra R A₂] (e : A₁ ≃ₐ[R] A₂),
  (MvPolynomial.mapAlgEquiv σ e).symm = MvPolynomial.mapAlgEquiv σ e.symm
items.informal_description: Given an $ R $-algebra equivalence $ e : A₁ ≃ₐ[R] A₂ $, the inverse of the induced multivariate polynomial ring equivalence $ A₁[σ] ≃ₐ[R] A₂[σ] $ (constructed by applying $ e $ coefficient-wise) is equal to the multivariate polynomial ring equivalence induced by the inverse algebra equivalence $ e^{-1} : A₂ ≃ₐ[R] A₁ $.

items.informal_name: Inverse of Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials over Unit Type
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u) [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : Polynomial R),
  (MvPolynomial.pUnitAlgEquiv R).symm p = Polynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C (MvPolynomial.X PUnit.unit) p
items.informal_description: The inverse of the algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ and the univariate polynomial ring $ R[X] $ maps a polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ to its representation in $ R[\mathsf{PUnit}] $ by substituting the indeterminate $ X $ with the single variable $ X(\mathsf{PUnit}.\mathsf{unit}) $ in the multivariate ring, using the constant polynomial embedding $ \mathsf{C} $ for coefficients.

items.informal_name: Inverse of the Equivalence for Polynomials with Restricted Support
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : DecidableEq κ] [inst_1 : CommRing R] [inst_2 : DecidableEq R]
  (p : ι → MvPolynomial κ R),
  ((FirstOrder.Ring.mvPolynomialSupportLEEquiv fun i => (p i).support).symm fun i =>
      MvPolynomial.coeff (↑i.snd) (p i.fst)) =
    ⟨p, ⋯⟩
items.informal_description: The inverse of the equivalence between polynomials with supports contained in specified finite monomial sets and coefficient functions reconstructs the original polynomial by setting coefficients outside the specified monomials to zero. For any family of polynomials $ p_i $ with supports in finite sets $ S_i $, applying the inverse equivalence to the coefficient functions $ (p_i.\text{coeff}(m))_{m \in S_i} $ yields the original family $ p $ along with the proof that each support is contained in its respective $ S_i $.
